labs.title: Configure a virtual network with subnets and an NSG
labs.summary: Create a VNet with web and data subnets, create an NSG, allow HTTPS to the web subnet, and keep the data subnet private.
labs.scenario: Fabrikam needs a small two-tier network. In the simulated Azure portal, create **vnet-app-prod** with address space **10.20.0.0/16** and two non-overlapping subnets: **snet-web 10.20.1.0/24** and **snet-data 10.20.2.0/24**. Create **nsg-web**, add an inbound rule allowing **HTTPS (443)** from the **Internet** service tag at priority **100**, and associate **nsg-web** with **snet-web** only. Review optional peering with **vnet-hub (10.0.0.0/16)** to see why address spaces must not overlap.
learningObjectives: Plan a virtual network address space
Add an HTTPS NSG rule with priority
Associate an NSG only to the internet-facing subnet
prerequisites: Know virtual network and NSG basics

steps.title: Open the virtual network wizard
steps.explanation: The wizard groups Basics, Security, IP addresses, Tags, and Review + create.

steps.title: Create vnet-app-prod and subnets
steps.instruction: Use **rg-network-prod**, name `vnet-app-prod`, **(Europe) West Europe**, **Address space** `10.20.0.0/16`, **snet-web address range** `10.20.1.0/24`, and **snet-data address range** `10.20.2.0/24`; select **Review + create** and **Create**.
steps.explanation: Subnet ranges must sit inside the VNet space and not overlap.

steps.title: Create nsg-web
steps.instruction: Open **Network security groups**, select **Create**, and create **nsg-web** in **rg-network-prod** and **(Europe) West Europe**.
steps.explanation: A separate web NSG avoids applying internet rules to the data subnet.

steps.title: Allow HTTPS from Internet
steps.instruction: In **nsg-web > Inbound security rules**, select **Add**. Set **Source** **Service Tag**, **Source service tag** **Internet**, **Service** **HTTPS**, **Destination port ranges** `443`, **Protocol** **TCP**, **Action** **Allow**, **Priority** `100`, **Name** `Allow-HTTPS-Internet`, then **Add**.
steps.explanation: Priority 100 is evaluated before default inbound rules such as AllowVnetInBound and DenyAllInBound 65500.

steps.title: Associate nsg-web with snet-web
steps.instruction: Open **nsg-web > Subnets**, select **Associate**, choose **Virtual network** `vnet-app-prod`, **Subnet** `snet-web`, then **OK**.
steps.explanation: Only the web subnet should receive the internet-facing HTTPS rule.

finalRules.description: snet-data is not associated with nsg-web
finalRules.failureFeedback: Do not associate nsg-web with snet-data.

finalRules.description: Web subnet has nsg-web and only HTTPS is exposed

labs.solution:
1. Select **Virtual networks** > **Create**.
2. Create `vnet-app-prod` in **rg-network-prod** with address space `10.20.0.0/16`, `snet-web` as `10.20.1.0/24`, and `snet-data` as `10.20.2.0/24`.
3. Select **Network security groups** > **Create** and create `nsg-web`.
4. In **nsg-web > Inbound security rules**, select **Add** and allow **HTTPS** from **Internet** on TCP `443` at priority `100` with name `Allow-HTTPS-Internet`.
5. In **nsg-web > Subnets**, select **Associate**, choose `vnet-app-prod` and `snet-web`, then **OK**.
